clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman with significant family history of aortic and brain aneurysms presented to the ED with acute onset abdominal pain, back pain, and chest pain. She initially attributed symptoms to her IBS and attempted self-treatment with an enema without relief. Symptoms persisted for 12 hours and evolved to include pain radiating from abdomen to back and up into chest, prompting ED evaluation. On presentation, she had elevated systolic blood pressure (170/68) with diffuse abdominal tenderness but no pulse deficits on physical examination. The ADD-RS (Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score) risk stratification identified her as high risk, leading to CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast. Imaging confirmed Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the aortic bifurcation. She was immediately started on medical management with nicardipine infusion (systolic pressure goal <120 mmHg) and esmolol infusion (heart rate goal <60 bpm). Cardiothoracic Surgery was consulted and she underwent emergency operative intervention. She made a complete recovery and was discharged after 8 days of hospitalization.
